question: What two broad categories does the deep-learning dialogue systems survey use to organize existing work, and which future research directions does it highlight?
Is there an overview paper that splits conversational agents into goal-driven and chit-chat types and reviews how neural methods have changed each kind?
How does Meena's Sensibleness and Specificity Average (SSA) metric relate to perplexity, and what does that correlation suggest about reaching human-level conversation quality?
Which work trains a 2.6-billion-parameter conversational model on filtered social media threads by just minimizing perplexity, and shows perplexity tracks human ratings of reply quality?
How does LaMDA improve safety and groundedness beyond what scaling alone achieves, for example by fine-tuning on crowdworker labels and consulting external tools like a calculator?
Which work fine-tunes a 137B-parameter conversational model with crowdworker labels to filter unsafe replies and lets it call a search tool, translator, and calculator to back up its facts?
According to the open-domain chatbot recipes work, which conversational skills and generation-strategy choices matter besides simply scaling up parameters and training data?
Which paper argues that mixing engagement, empathy, knowledge, and a stable persona with good decoding choices matters as much as size, releasing 90M to 9.4B parameter models?
How does the alignment-based RNN with attention jointly predict intents and slot labels on ATIS, and how much does joint training improve over separate models?
Which ATIS study adapts encoder-decoder models, exploiting the explicit word-to-label alignment, to simultaneously classify what a user wants and tag each word of the query?
How does the Joint BERT model for intent classification and slot filling compare with attention-based RNN and slot-gated models on sentence-level semantic frame accuracy?
Which paper fine-tunes a large pretrained bidirectional Transformer to simultaneously predict a user's goal and tag query words, tackling weak generalization from small labeled datasets?
How does the Snips Voice Platform keep spoken language understanding private by design while still running speech recognition and NLU in real time on IoT hardware?

Which work describes an on-device assistant stack doing speech recognition and command interpretation on tiny IoT chips without ever gathering personal user data, plus a way to synthesize training data?
Why does the BI-LSTM-CRF model outperform plain LSTM and CRF taggers on POS, chunking, and NER, in terms of using past and future features and sentence-level tag information?

Which paper combines a recurrent network reading sentences forward and backward with a structured output layer modeling label transitions, applying it to part-of-speech, chunking, and entity recognition benchmarks?
How does L-TapNet use label name semantics, and how does collapsed dependency transfer let CRF transition scores carry over to unseen domains in few-shot slot tagging?

Which work tackles finding entity spans in user utterances from just one or a few example sentences by reusing generic transition patterns between categories across domains and scoring words against embeddings of category names?
How does the end-to-end trainable neural task-oriented dialogue model collect its data with a pipelined Wizard-of-Oz framework, and in which domain was it evaluated?
Which early work builds a single neural text-in/text-out model that helps people find restaurants, trained on conversations gathered through a crowdsourced scheme where humans play the system?
How does the Neural Belief Tracker (NBT) use pre-trained word vectors to avoid relying on hand-crafted semantic lexicons or separate spoken language understanding modules?
Which model infers what the user wants turn by turn by composing pretrained word embeddings of the utterance and context, removing the need for hand-built lexicons or separate understanding modules?
How was the MultiWOZ dataset collected through crowdsourcing without professional annotators, and what benchmark tasks were reported on it as baselines?

Which crowdsourced corpus of roughly 10k written conversations between two people across several topics comes annotated with dialogue acts and belief states, an order of magnitude bigger than earlier ones?
In the deep reinforcement learning approach to dialogue generation, what three reward properties are optimized when simulating conversations between two agents with policy gradients?
Which work has two simulated agents talk to each other and uses policy gradients to reward informative, coherent, easy-to-answer turns so chatbots plan for long-term conversation success?
How does TRADE use a copy mechanism and a slot gate to generate dialogue states, enabling zero-shot tracking for domains unseen during training?
Which belief tracking model produces (domain, slot, value) triples by copying words from the conversation, sharing all of its components across domains so it works zero-shot on new ones?
How does the Schema-Guided Dialogue (SGD) dataset's paradigm let one model support new services zero-shot by conditioning on natural language descriptions of intents and slots?
Which 16k-conversation corpus spanning 16 domains lets virtual assistants handle new APIs without retraining by feeding in natural-language descriptions of each service's intents and slots?
In the original word2vec paper, how do the CBOW and Skip-gram architectures learn high-quality word vectors from a 1.6-billion-word corpus within a day?
Which paper introduced two simple log-linear architectures that learn continuous word vectors from over a billion words within a single day, judged on syntactic and semantic analogy questions?
How do negative sampling and subsampling of frequent words improve the Skip-gram word2vec vectors, and how does the method handle phrases like 'Air Canada'?

Which follow-up to the original word-embedding model replaces hierarchical softmax with a simpler sampling-based objective, downsamples common words, and learns vectors for idiomatic multi-word expressions?
How does Sentence-BERT (SBERT) use siamese and triplet network structures to make semantic similarity search over 10,000 sentences take seconds instead of hours?
Which work trains a pretrained Transformer encoder in a twin-tower setup so every input text maps to one vector comparable by cosine similarity, cutting similarity search from hours to seconds?
How does Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) train its dual-encoder from a modest number of question-passage pairs, and how much does it beat BM25 on top-20 accuracy?
Which work shows that a simple pair of BERT encoders for questions and Wikipedia text chunks, trained on few examples, beats BM25 at fetching supporting text for trivia-style questions?
How does ELMo derive word vectors from the internal states of a deep bidirectional language model, and why does mixing all of its layers help downstream tasks?

Which work builds word vectors that change with surrounding context by combining every internal layer of a pretrained forward-and-backward language model, boosting six benchmarks like sentiment and entailment?
How is the RNN Encoder-Decoder used to score phrase pairs as an additional feature in a phrase-based statistical machine translation system?

Which paper uses two jointly trained recurrent networks, one compressing a source sequence into a fixed-size vector and one expanding it back out, to add a scoring feature to a log-linear translation system?
In the 'NLP (almost) from scratch' work, how does one unified neural architecture handle POS tagging, chunking, NER, and semantic role labeling without task-specific features?
Which work trains one shared neural architecture to label semantic roles, named entities, chunks, and parts of speech, learning features from large unlabeled text instead of hand-engineered inputs?
How does the gradient norm clipping proposal for RNNs deal with exploding gradients, and what soft constraint does it suggest for the vanishing gradient problem?
Which paper analyzes why gradients blow up or shrink in sequence models from geometric and dynamical-systems viewpoints and proposes rescaling the gradient whenever its norm gets too large?
In the empirical GRU versus LSTM comparison, how did these gated units fare against traditional tanh units on polyphonic music and speech signal modeling?
Which study pits LSTM against a newer, lighter cell and plain tanh units on polyphonic music and speech signal tasks, finding the newer cell about as good as LSTM?
How does ConVEx's pairwise cloze pretraining objective on Reddit match the slot-labeling task, and why does it only fine-tune the decoding layers?
Which approach pretrains on a Reddit fill-in-the-blank task between sentence pairs so that, with most weights frozen, tuning only the top layers yields strong span tagging from very few examples?
How does the reading comprehension approach to dialog state tracking point to slot values in the conversation instead of predicting over a closed ontology?
Which work treats figuring out a user's current goals in a conversation as a question-answering problem over the dialogue history, pointing at value spans instead of choosing from a fixed ontology?
How do instruction-tuned LLMs perform at explicit belief state tracking versus specialized models when evaluated on established task-oriented dialogue benchmarks with external databases?
Which study tests instruction-following chat models on multi-turn booking-style benchmarks and finds they lag specialized trackers but can still finish the task when handed the right slot values?
How was DialoGPT trained on 147M Reddit comment-chain exchanges, and how does its response quality compare to humans in single-turn evaluation?
Which work released a Transformer reply model trained on 147 million Reddit comment-thread exchanges from 2005 to 2017 that nearly matches humans in single-turn evaluations?
In the seq2seq LSTM translation paper, why does reversing the word order of source sentences markedly improve English-to-French translation performance?
Which paper translates English to French by encoding the input with one deep LSTM into a fixed vector and decoding with another, noting that reversing source word order helps a lot?
How does the Bahdanau attention model (RNNsearch) soft-search over source positions to remove the fixed-length vector bottleneck of basic encoder-decoder translation?

Which translation paper argues that compressing the whole input sentence into one fixed-size vector limits performance, and lets the decoder softly search for relevant source words for each output word?
How do the global and local attention mechanisms in Luong attention for neural machine translation differ, and how much BLEU does local attention add on English-German WMT?
Which translation study contrasts a mechanism that looks at every source word with one that focuses on a small window of source positions, setting a new WMT'15 English-to-German record?
How does the Neural Conversational Model apply the seq2seq framework to IT helpdesk and movie subtitle data, and what failure mode around consistency did it show?
Which early paper simply trains a sequence-mapping network to predict the next utterance, testing it on an IT helpdesk dataset and noisy movie subtitles, where it lacked a consistent personality?
How does using Maximum Mutual Information (MMI) as the training objective reduce generic responses like 'I don't know' in seq2seq conversation models?
Which paper swaps the usual likelihood criterion for one that rewards replies being informative about the input message, so chat systems stop defaulting to 'I don't know'?
How does the Transformer dispense with recurrence and convolution entirely, and why does this make it more parallelizable and faster to train for translation?

Which architecture paper drops recurrent and convolutional layers altogether, letting each token directly weigh every other token, and hits 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-German using eight GPUs for 3.5 days?
How does byte pair encoding (BPE) segmentation into subword units enable open-vocabulary neural machine translation without a back-off dictionary?

Which translation paper repurposes a data compression algorithm to split infrequent and unseen words into smaller pieces, removing the need for a back-off dictionary on English-German and English-Russian?
How does SentencePiece train subword models directly from raw sentences rather than requiring pre-tokenized input, and why does that make it language independent?

Which open-source library, with C++ and Python bindings, learns a vocabulary of word fragments directly from raw, unsegmented sentences, avoiding language-specific pre-splitting, and is validated on English-Japanese translation?
